config.enabled.name: Enable SDV-Radiance
config.enabled.tooltip: Master switch for the whole post-processing pipeline.
config.preset.hint: Tip: presets and your saved custom looks live in the on-screen tuner (open with the tuner hotkey, default F6). It previews live and always stays in sync.
config.preset.name: Quick preset
config.preset.tooltip: Picks a ready-made look. It replaces the bloom and colour settings below, so reopen the menu to see the new values.
config.togglekey.name: Toggle effects on/off
config.togglekey.tooltip: Instantly turn the whole post-processing stack on or off (quick A/B compare while playing).
config.tunerkey.name: Open live tuner
config.tunerkey.tooltip: Open the on-screen tuner overlay to adjust the look while seeing the scene live.
config.opentuner.name: Open the Radiance tuner
config.opentuner.tooltip: Opens the full F6 tuner, with every setting, once you close this menu. Handy on phones. The tick clears itself, which is normal.
config.inspectdrawkey.name: Ask what drew this pixel
config.inspectdrawkey.tooltip: Point at something that looks wrong and press this. The SMAPI console lists what drew that spot and how much it was scaled up (the game's own art is always 4). No key until you set one.
tuner.title: SDV-Radiance Tuner
tuner.packlooks.desc: Mods you have installed offer these. Pick one to try it on: you see what it changes before anything is kept.
tuner.suggested.on: Suggested: on (new things always start off).
tuner.share.desc: A short code with your settings. Share it, or paste someone else's.
tuner.share.copiedall: Copied, with your performance settings in it. {{count}} setting(s) travel with it.
tuner.share.nothing: Nothing to share yet. You haven't changed any settings.
help.share.copy: Copies a code for your current look. Only the settings you changed go in, so it stays short.
help.share.copyall: Same, but your performance settings go in too. Those change how smooth the game runs, not how it looks, so they are left out otherwise.
help.share.paste: Try a look someone shared. It shows right away, and nothing is saved until you press Keep it.
tuner.share.trial: You are looking at this code now. It changes {{count}} setting(s):
tuner.share.newer: {{count}} setting(s) in it come from a newer version and are skipped.
tuner.share.lutmissing: It uses a colour table called "{{name}}" that is not on this computer, so your colours stay as they are.
tuner.share.closeputsback: Closing the panel puts your look back, unless you have changed something else since.
tuner.share.kept: Code kept: {{count}} setting(s) changed. Your look from before is saved as a chip.
tuner.share.same: That code matches what you already have.
tuner.share.bad.notours: That is not an SDV-Radiance code. They begin with RAD.
tuner.share.bad.scope: That code was made by a newer version of the mod, which this one cannot open yet.
tuner.share.bad.typo: That code is missing a character or has one too many. Copy the whole thing and try again.
help.reset.all: Puts every setting back to the mod's defaults, like a fresh install. Your saved looks stay, and it asks first.
tuner.reset.ask: Put every setting back to the default? This cannot be undone. Your saved looks are kept, so a look you saved can be loaded again afterwards.
tuner.cat.looks.desc: Pick a ready-made look, save your own, or try one another mod offers.
tuner.cat.light.desc: The sun's shadows, lamps at night, light through windows and the glow around bright things.
tuner.cat.water.desc: How lakes, rivers and the sea look and move, and what they reflect.
tuner.cat.weather.desc: Rain, snow, wind, storms, fog and the sky over it all.
tuner.cat.nature.desc: Plants in the wind and the little things in the air: fireflies, petals, dust, sparks.
tuner.cat.picture.desc: Colour, lens effects, smoothing the pixel art, and the camera.
tuner.cat.perf.desc: Make it run smoothly on your machine, and see what it costs here.
tuner.layout.ask: Settings are now grouped by what you see: light, water, weather and so on, with a search box. Your settings stay exactly as they are, and you can switch at any time at the top of this menu.
tuner.layout.asktitle: A new layout for this menu
tuner.helpbar.idle: Point at a setting to see what it does. Most groups show the game without it and with it.
help.density: How much room the menu leaves between its rows and groups.
help.textsize: Makes the menu's text smaller or larger. The menu grows or shrinks with it, so nothing gets cut off.
help.glassshade: How dark the glass is over the game. Darker makes the words easier to read over a bright scene.
help.glasslight: Pale glass with dark words, for when the dark glass is hard to read.
tuner.packlooks.none: None of the mods you have installed offers a look yet. When one does, it shows up here.
tuner.search.none: Nothing matches. Try a shorter word.
tuner.deletelook.ask: Delete the look "{{name}}"? It cannot be brought back.
tuner.hint: Drag: preview  •  wheel: scroll  •  right-click a look: delete  •  Esc: save
tuner.section.foldhint: Click to fold this group away, or to open it again.
tuner.hide.sectionhint: Hide this group. Its switches turn off too. You can bring it back from the bottom of the page.
tuner.hide.sectionhint.keep: Hide this group. Its settings keep working as they are now. You can bring it back from the bottom of the page.
tuner.hide.switchhint: Hide this switch. It turns off too. You can bring it back from the bottom of the page.
tuner.hidden.title: Hidden on this page ({{count}})
tuner.resethover: Changed from the default ({{default}}). Right-click to put it back.
tuner.resethover.plain: Changed from the default. Right-click to put it back.
config.bloom.enabled.name: Enable bloom
config.bloom.enabled.tooltip: Glow around bright areas such as lamps and sunlight.
config.bloom.threshold.name: Bloom threshold
config.bloom.intensity.name: Bloom intensity
config.bloom.emissiveboost.name: Colored-light glow
config.weather.aurora.name: Aurora on winter nights
config.weather.aurora.tooltip: On clear winter nights, slow green and violet lights drift across the sky reflected in the water. You only see it in water, since the camera never shows the sky.
config.weather.aurorastrength.name: Aurora strength
config.weather.aurorastrength.tooltip: How bright the aurora is. 1 is the default, and it goes up to 2 because open water only shows a faint part of it.
config.weather.snowglint.name: Snow glitters in the sun
config.weather.snowglint.tooltip: On clear winter days, snowflakes catch the sun and twinkle, less in shade and not at all under cloud. Only costs anything outdoors on winter days. 0 keeps the snow still.
config.weather.shootingstars.name: Shooting stars
config.weather.shootingstars.tooltip: Now and then on a clear night, a shooting star crosses the sky reflected in the water. About one a minute while you are near water, in any season.
config.weather.shootingstarfrequency.too: How often a shooting star crosses the night water. 1 is about one a minute, 2 is twice as often, 4 is four times as often.
config.weather.waternightstars.name: Stars on the water
config.weather.waternightstars.tooltip: Twinkling starlight on the water after dusk. Off keeps night water plain but leaves the moonlight and lamp glimmer.
config.weather.waternightstarsamount.nam: Stars on the water: how many
config.weather.waternightstarsamount.too: How many stars twinkle on the water on a clear night. 1 is the default, 2 is twice as many, 0 shows none.
config.weather.gameweatherplaintint.name: Game's weather over water in plain grey
config.weather.gameweatherplaintint.tool: The game's own rain, snow and leaves turn a plain grey where they pass over water, matching the light around them. Off keeps the game's colour for them (blue in rain).
config.weather.windyspells.name: Windy spells
config.weather.windyspells.tooltip: Two or three windy spells a day, each building up and dying down over about twenty minutes, with trees leaning harder, rain and leaves blowing sideways and clouds moving faster. Same for everyone in co-op. Off keeps the normal wind.
config.weather.windyspellsstrength.name: Windy spell strength
config.weather.windyspellsstrength.toolt: How much stronger than normal the wind gets at a spell's peak, 1.25 to 3 times.
config.bloom.emissiveboost.tooltip: Lets coloured lights like lit windows, lava, flames and crystals glow even when they are not very bright. White and grey never glow from this, so snow and white walls stay calm. 0 is off.
config.colorgrade.enabled.name: Enable color grading
config.colorgrade.auto.name: Auto mood (time / weather / season)
config.colorgrade.auto.tooltip: Changes warmth and colour on its own. Warm at sunset, cool at night, cooler and duller in rain or snow, and a little different each season.
config.colorgrade.strength.name: Strength
config.colorgrade.contrast.name: Contrast
config.colorgrade.saturation.name: Saturation
config.colorgrade.temperature.name: Temperature (warm / cool)
config.colorgrade.temperature.tooltip: Negative = cooler/bluer, positive = warmer/oranger. Added on top of the auto mood.
config.colorgrade.brightness.name: Brightness
config.colorgrade.tonemap.name: Filmic tone mapping (ACES)
config.colorgrade.tonemap.tooltip: Off by default. It only really helps when Brightness is above 1, otherwise it can make the picture look muddy.
config.colorgrade.bluelight.name: Blue-light filter
config.colorgrade.bluelight.tooltip: Warms the picture to rest your eyes, like a night-light mode. 0 is off. Works even with colour grading off.
help.lutamount: How strongly the chosen look is mixed in. 0 is off. It sits on top of the colour sliders and does not replace them.
config.colorgrade.lut.name: Look (colour LUT)
config.colorgrade.lut.tooltip: A ready-made look on top of the colour sliders, and none of them turn dark rooms grey. To add your own, put a 1024x32 LUT strip in the radiance-luts folder next to your saves and it shows up here next launch (mod updates won't delete it).
config.colorgrade.lutamount.name: Look strength
config.colorgrade.lutamount.tooltip: How much of the look to apply. 0 is off.
config.godrays.enabled.name: Enable lamp shafts (god rays)
config.godrays.enabled.tooltip: Light beams from lamps, torches and fires shining past doorways, window frames or trees. Off by default and needs the flood lighting on. Sun shafts are a separate switch below.
config.godrays.intensity.name: Intensity
config.fog.enabled.name: Enable day fog
config.fog.enabled.tooltip: Drifting mist during the day that fades out at dusk.
config.fog.nightmist.name: Enable night mist
config.fog.nightmist.tooltip: Thin blue wisps of mist after dusk, outdoors in clear weather. They fade in as the day fog fades out.
config.fog.nightmistdensity.name: Night mist intensity
config.fog.minemist.name: Mist in the mine
config.fog.minemist.tooltip: Lays the mod's drifting mist over foggy mine levels, which normally just have a flat fog that never moves. 0 keeps the mines as they were.
config.fog.nightmistcoverage.name: Night mist amount
config.fog.nightmistspeed.name: Night mist drift speed
config.fog.nightmistlampglow.name: Night mist glows near lamps
config.fog.nightmistlampglow.tooltip: Night mist drifting past a lamp picks up its light, like mist around a street lamp. Cheap to run. 0 keeps the mist plain blue.
config.fog.coverage.name: Fog amount
config.fog.coverage.tooltip: How much of the screen the wisps occupy.
config.fog.density.tooltip: How strongly each wisp tints the scene.
config.fog.density.name: Density
config.fog.scale.name: Mist scale
config.fog.speed.name: Drift speed
config.fog.morningonly.name: Morning fog only
config.fog.morningonly.tooltip: Day fog only in the morning, thickest at dawn and gone by the hour set below. Off keeps the fog all day.
config.fog.morninglifthour.name: Morning fog gone by (hour)
config.fog.morninglifthour.tooltip: The hour the morning fog is fully gone, 7 to 12. It thins out over the hour and a half before.
tuner.gameweatherplaintint: Game's weather over water: plain grey
help.waterglitterpath: Stretches the water glints toward the sun and gathers them on its side of the screen when it is low. 0 keeps the old round, even glitter.
config.water.glitterpath.name: Glitter follows the sun
config.water.glitterpath.tooltip: Water glints stretch out toward the sun, most when it is low, and gather on its side of the screen at sunrise and sunset. No extra cost. 0 keeps the old round, even glitter.
help.windowreflectionstrength: How clearly a window reflects whoever stands in front of it by day, when the room behind the glass is dark.
help.windowreflectionnight: The same after dusk, when the window is lit from inside. 0 stops the reflection once it lights up.
help.windowvehicleglass: How clearly you and the street show in the bus windows. Shop windows use the slider above.
help.windowsheen: A faint wash of sky colour and two diagonal streaks on window glass, even when nobody is near. 0 leaves the glass as the map drew it.
help.windowglare: A soft spot of light that slides across the glass as you walk past. 0 turns it off.
help.windowscene: The ground and buildings in front of a window show faintly in the glass, like a mirror. 0 turns it off.
help.windowlightglow: Nearby lamps show as soft coloured spots in the windows facing them, fading with distance. Brightest at night, dimmer at midday. 0 turns it off.
config.lighting.windowreflectionstrength: How clearly windows reflect whoever stands in front of them by day. Mirrors always stay stronger than plain glass, and plain glass stronger than house windows.
config.lighting.windowreflectionnight.to: Reflection strength after dusk, usually lower than by day since a lit window shows the room inside. 0 stops the reflection once the window lights up.
config.lighting.windowvehicleglass.name: Bus glass
config.lighting.windowvehicleglass.toolt: How much vehicle glass reflects, like the bus windows and windscreen. 0 leaves just the sky tint and glare.
config.lighting.windowsheen.name: Sky in the glass
config.lighting.windowsheen.tooltip: How much sky colour window glass shows, brighter near the top, with two diagonal streaks. It fades after dusk when windows light up. 0 leaves the glass as the map drew it.
config.lighting.windowglare.name: Glare on the glass
config.lighting.windowglare.tooltip: A soft spot of light that slides across window glass as it moves across the screen, so windows look like real glass. Fades after dusk. 0 turns it off.
config.lighting.windowscene.name: The street in the glass
config.lighting.windowscene.tooltip: How clearly the ground and buildings in front of a window show in its glass, flipped like a mirror. Trees, people and animals are not included (people get their own reflection). 0 turns it off.
config.lighting.windowlightglow.name: Lamps in the glass
config.lighting.windowlightglow.tooltip: How brightly lamps show in the windows facing them, as soft coloured spots that fade with distance. Brightest after dark and about a third of that at midday. 0 turns it off.
tuner.waterhere.always: Water here: always on (outdoor / level water)
config.tiltshift.enabled.name: Enable tilt-shift
config.tiltshift.enabled.tooltip: Keep a sharp band across the middle and blur the top and bottom (fake miniature / depth-of-field look).
config.tiltshift.mode.name: Focus shape
config.tiltshift.mode.tooltip: Bands = sharp middle strip, blurred top & bottom. Radial = sharp circle around the player, blurred outward.
config.tiltshift.radius.name: Sharp circle size (radial)
config.tiltshift.radius.tooltip: Radial mode only: how big the in-focus circle around the player is before it blurs outward.
config.tiltshift.feather.name: Edge softness
config.tiltshift.feather.tooltip: How gradually the image eases from sharp to blurred. Higher is softer, removing the hard band edge.
config.tiltshift.strength.name: Blur strength
config.tiltshift.top.name: Top blur amount
config.tiltshift.bottom.name: Bottom blur amount
config.tiltshift.indoor.name: Indoor amount
config.tiltshift.indoor.tooltip: How much of the blur stays indoors. 0 keeps rooms evenly sharp, 1 blurs them the same as outside.
config.cloudshadow.hidevanilla.name: Hide vanilla cloud shadows
config.cloudshadow.hidevanilla.tooltip: Remove the base game's drifting Cloud-critter shadows (so only this mod's cloud shadows show).
config.cloudshadow.enabled.name: Enable cloud shadows
config.cloudshadow.enabled.tooltip: Soft shadows of drifting clouds moving across the ground (outdoors only).
config.cloudshadow.opacity.name: Opacity
config.cloudshadow.coverage.name: Coverage
config.cloudshadow.scale.name: Cloud size
config.cloudshadow.count.name: Cloud count
config.cloudshadow.count.tooltip: How many cloud banks share the screen. Low is a few big ones, high is many small puffs.
config.cloudshadow.speed.name: Drift speed
config.cloudshadow.stormwarning.name: Before the rain
config.cloudshadow.stormwarning.tooltip: On the afternoon before rain or snow, clouds slowly build up and the light gets a little cooler. 0 turns it off.
config.water.enabled.name: Enable water shimmer
config.water.enabled.tooltip: Gentle ripple and sparkle on water tiles. Subtle, since the game already animates its water. Experimental.
config.water.strength.name: Ripple strength
config.water.speed.name: Ripple speed
config.water.sparkle.name: Sparkle
config.water.sparkleday.name: Sparkle by day
config.water.sparkleday.tooltip: Glints on the water in the daytime. Night glints have their own switch.
config.water.sparklenight.name: Sparkle at night
config.water.sparklenight.tooltip: Glints on the water after dusk. Stars, moonlight and lamp glimmer have their own switches.
config.water.sparkledensity.name: Sparkle amount
config.water.sparkledensity.tooltip: How many glints dot the water (their size changes with it). 1.0 is the original busy look, lower is calmer.
config.water.sparklecloud.name: Clouds dim the sparkle
config.water.sparklecloud.tooltip: Cloud shadows passing over water dim the glitter, the same way they darken the ground. Off keeps the glitter under clouds.
config.water.caustics.name: Caustics
config.water.caustics.tooltip: The wobbly light pattern on the bottom of shallow water, strongest near the shore. Fades out at night and in bad weather.
config.water.causticsstrength.name: Caustics strength
config.water.reflection.name: Water reflection
config.water.reflection.tooltip: Faintly reflects the scene above onto the water for a wet, shiny look. Subtle on purpose. Experimental.
config.water.reflectstrength.name: Reflection strength
config.water.indoors.name: Water effect indoors
config.water.indoors.tooltip: Water effect inside houses and cabins, including house mods. Turn it off if a mod's decorative water should not ripple. Caves, mines, the sewer and the bathhouse always keep it.
config.vignette.enabled.name: Enable vignette
config.vignette.enabled.tooltip: Darken the screen edges for a cinematic frame.
config.vignette.strength.name: Vignette strength
config.ca.enabled.name: Enable chromatic aberration
config.ca.enabled.tooltip: Subtle color fringing toward the edges, like a camera lens. Keep it low on pixel art.
config.ca.strength.name: Aberration strength
config.lighting.flood.name: Flood GI lighting
config.lighting.flood.tooltip: Light from lamps and the sky spreads across the map and gets blocked by things, so trees and buildings cast soft shade, lamps light around corners and windows glow at night. Replaces the classic lighting below.
config.lighting.gimodel.name: GI model
config.lighting.gimodel.tooltip: How the lighting is worked out. Flood is the classic one. Radiance cascades runs on the graphics card and its shade follows the shape of whatever is in the way more closely. Switching fades over smoothly.
config.lighting.relief.name: Sprite relief
config.lighting.relief.tooltip: Sides of trees, buildings, characters and objects that face a lamp or the sun get a bit brighter, and the far sides a bit darker. Needs the flood lighting and uses up to 192 MB of video memory.
config.lighting.reliefstrength.name: Relief from lamps
config.lighting.reliefstrength.tooltip: How far a lamp's light leans across a sprite: 0 is flat, 1 is the full lean.
config.lighting.reliefhalfres.name: Relief at half size
config.lighting.reliefhalfres.tooltip: Draws the sprite relief at half size, which looks the same but costs about a quarter as much. Helps most on wide or high resolution screens. Off draws it at full size.
config.lighting.reliefsun.name: Relief from the sun
config.lighting.reliefsun.tooltip: How much the sun adds to the sprite relief outdoors in the day. The lit side is the one opposite the shadows.
config.lighting.reliefrim.name: Rim light from lamps
config.lighting.reliefrim.tooltip: A thin bright edge in a lamp's colour on the side of a sprite facing it, so people and trees look lit from that side. Needs the sprite relief.
config.lighting.leafshimmer.name: Leaves catch the light
config.lighting.leafshimmer.tooltip: Patches of leaves catch and lose the light as if flipping in the wind, without moving the art. Shows less on autumn trees and needs the sprite relief.
config.lighting.floodstrength.name: Flood lighting strength
config.lighting.floodstrength.tooltip: How strongly the flood lighting shades the scene. Lower keeps the vanilla look with a hint of shading.
config.lighting.floodshadow.name: Per-light shadow strength
config.lighting.floodshadow.tooltip: How dark it gets where a wall, tree, or character blocks a lamp's light. Every light source casts its own soft shadows.
config.lighting.colourbleed.name: Bounced light takes the colour of surfaces
config.lighting.colourbleed.tooltip: Bounced light picks up the colour of what it hits, so a red barn tints the ground beside it red and a green field tints things in it green. Changes colour only, not brightness. 0 is off.
config.lighting.carriedbounce.name: Carried lights feed the bounce
config.lighting.carriedbounce.tooltip: Lets a light you carry (a glow ring, a torch, a companion's light) brighten the whole room, not just the ground around you. Off, the room only gets light from its own lamps and it doesn't shift as you walk. On by default.
config.lighting.shadowcarve.name: Shadow cuts into the glow
config.lighting.shadowcarve.tooltip: How much a lamp shadow cuts into the game's own round glow around lamps. 0 keeps the glow round, 1 cuts the shadow all the way through it.
config.lighting.shadowsoftness.name: Shadow edge softness
config.lighting.shadowsoftness.tooltip: How blurry a lamp shadow's edge gets as it stretches away from what casts it. 0 is a sharp edge, 1 blurs about a quarter of a tile, 2 blurs up to a whole tile.
config.lighting.shadowdetail.name: Lamp shadow detail
config.lighting.shadowdetail.tooltip: How detailed lamp shadows are. It costs more the more lamps are on screen, so lower this first if busy places stutter. 0 is faster, 1 catches thin things like fence posts.
config.lighting.shadowshared.name: Share lamp shadow detail
config.lighting.shadowshared.tooltip: When several lamps light the same spot, they share the shadow detail instead of each one getting the full amount. Two lamps still get full detail, more than that share it. Helps most in small rooms full of lamps.
config.lighting.shadowsharp.name: Sharp lamp shadow edges
config.lighting.shadowsharp.tooltip: Draws lamp shadows at full screen resolution for the sharpest edge. Off runs noticeably lighter and most people can't tell the two apart. Stand by a keg or fence post near a lamp and flip it to compare.
config.lighting.shadowcache.name: Remember lamp shadows
config.lighting.shadowcache.tooltip: Remembers lamp shadows and only redraws them when something changes or you step onto a new tile, which saves a lot of work. Off redraws every lamp every frame. Turn it off if a lamp shadow seems to lag behind what casts it, and say where on the mod page.
config.lighting.wateredsoil.name: Watered soil sparkles
config.lighting.wateredsoil.tooltip: Watered soil sparkles here and there in the sun. Fades in the evening, in rain and at night. 0 turns it off.
config.lighting.enabled.name: Enable dynamic lighting
config.lighting.enabled.tooltip: Darkens unlit areas and adds warm pools of light around lamps, torches and fireplaces.
config.lighting.indoor.name: Indoor darkness
config.lighting.indoor.tooltip: How much darker rooms get, so lamps actually matter. The game keeps most rooms evenly bright. 0 = off.
config.lighting.night.name: Night darkness
config.lighting.night.tooltip: How dark it gets at night, outdoors and in rooms. Lamps and fires keep their full colour, so darker nights make them stand out more.
config.lighting.morning.name: Morning darkness
config.lighting.morning.tooltip: How dark the early morning stays (before 7:00). 0 means the room is bright when you wake up, higher means darker mornings.
config.lighting.indoorcolour.name: Indoor colour by hour
config.lighting.indoorcolour.tooltip: How much a room's colour follows the time of day, cool in the morning, warm before dark and blue at night. 1 is the usual look, 0 keeps the game's own colours (rooms still dim with the hour). If rooms look too cold, lower this rather than GI strength, which also changes the outdoors.
config.lighting.morningcool.name: Cool cast on clear mornings
config.lighting.morningcool.tooltip: How blue rooms look on a clear morning. 1 gives the same cool morning whatever the weather, 0 gives clear mornings no blue tint at all. Rainy and stormy mornings stay cool either way.
config.lighting.warmth.name: Light warmth
config.lighting.boost.name: Light brightness
config.lighting.radius.name: Light radius scale
config.lighting.shadows.name: Cast shadows
config.lighting.shadows.tooltip: Walls and buildings block light and cast soft shadows away from each lamp. Experimental.
config.lighting.shadowstrength.name: Shadow strength
config.lighting.silhouettes.name: Shadows shaped by fences and bushes
config.lighting.silhouettes.tooltip: Fences, bushes and boulders block lamp light in their real shape, so a torch behind a fence shines through the gaps. Off, each one blocks a whole tile and shadows look blockier.
config.lighting.props.name: Shadows from placed things
config.lighting.props.tooltip: Kegs, chests, machines, scarecrows, signs and furniture block lamp light, so they cast shadows at night too. Off, lamp light goes straight through them.
config.lighting.windoweffects.name: Window daylight and glow
config.lighting.windoweffects.tooltip: One switch for all of this mod's window effects, the daylight coming into rooms and the warm glow on house windows at night. Turn it off if another mod handles your windows.
config.lighting.windowopensnight.name: Lit windows push the night back
config.lighting.windowopensnight.tooltip: Lit town windows at night also light up the ground in front of the house instead of leaving it dark. Costs almost nothing. 0 turns it off.
config.lighting.lamphalo.name: Halo around lamps
config.lighting.lamphalo.tooltip: A wide, very faint ring around each lamp at night, like you see through a camera lens. 0 turns it off.
config.lighting.aquariumripple.name: Fish tanks light like water
config.lighting.aquariumripple.tooltip: Fish tanks cast slowly moving patches of light, like light through water, instead of one still circle. 0 keeps the still circle.
config.lighting.tvglow.name: TV screen light
config.lighting.tvglow.tooltip: When a show is on, the TV lights the room with a cool, slightly blue flicker. 0 keeps the game's own TV light.
config.lighting.windowbeam.name: Window beam and glass
config.lighting.windowbeam.tooltip: The part of window light you can see, the bright glass, the sunbeam and the patch of sun on the floor. Turn it off if another window mod already draws these. Rooms still get daylight from their windows either way.
config.lighting.windowdetail.name: Window detail
config.lighting.windowdetail.tooltip: Whole window lets the room's light brighten a window like everything else, as before. Keep detail holds back the brightening on windows, so bars, frames and curtains stay visible at midday. Nothing else in the room changes.
Same as above, but for every building that isn't your house, like shops, villagers' homes and the saloon. If your farmhouse looks fine but other homes look too bright, lower this one. 1 is the default.
config.lighting.windowdaylightstrength.t: How bright the glass, the sunbeam and the sun patch on the floor are. 1 is the default. Lower it if windows look washed out, raise it for a dim house.
config.lighting.windowreflection.name: Reflections in windows
config.lighting.windowreflection.tooltip: People walking past a window show up in the glass, clearly by day and faintly after dusk. Mirrors reflect fully, glass less, house windows least. The switch below turns it on indoors too.
Windows and glass inside buildings reflect the floor and anyone standing in front of them. Indoors it works the other way round, faint by day and mirror-like at night, so the day and night sliders below swap roles. Off reflects outdoors only.
config.shadows.enabled.name: Enable directional shadows
config.shadows.enabled.tooltip: Characters cast a soft shadow away from the sun that leans with the time of day. Outdoors, daytime and clear weather only. Experimental.
config.shadows.model.name: Shadow shapes
config.shadows.model.tooltip: Shadows 1.7 starts object shadows right at their base and lays four-legged animals' shadows flat on the ground. Shadows 1.6 lifts object shadows a little off the ground and stands animal shadows up like a person's. Only the shape changes, all other shadow fixes work in both.
config.shadows.strength.name: Shadow strength
config.shadows.strength.tooltip: How dark shadows are. Past 1 they keep getting darker, close to black at 3. Going past 1 costs nothing extra.
config.shadows.length.name: Shadow length
config.shadows.goldenhour.name: Golden hour
config.shadows.goldenhour.tooltip: How much longer shadows get in the first and last hour of sunlight. Midday is unchanged. 0 turns it off.
config.shadows.sunseason.name: Sun follows the season
config.shadows.sunseason.tooltip: How much the sun's height and the length of the day follow the season. Winter brings a low sun, long shadows and short days. 0 makes every day a summer day.
config.shadows.tint.name: Shadow colour
config.shadows.tint.tooltip: How much colour shadows pick up from around them, blue from the sky, grey in rain, warm indoors. 0 is plain black.
config.shadows.blur.name: Edge softness
config.shadows.objects.name: Shadows for trees & bushes
config.shadows.buildings.name: Shadows for buildings
config.shadows.objects.tooltip: Also cast leaning shadows from trees and bushes, not just characters.
config.shadows.fences.name: Fence shadows
config.shadows.fences.tooltip: Fences cast their shadows too, when trees & bushes cast theirs. Off, a fence casts none and everything else keeps its shadow.
config.shadows.player.name: Shadows for the player
config.shadows.player.tooltip: Whether you and your co-op partners cast a shadow. Off also removes the dark spot under your feet.
config.shadows.villagers.name: Shadows for villagers
config.shadows.villagers.tooltip: Whether villagers cast shadows. Also covers monsters, festival guests and NPCs from other mods.
config.shadows.farmanimals.name: Shadows for farm animals
config.shadows.farmanimals.tooltip: Whether the animals in your barns and coops cast.
config.shadows.creatures.name: Shadows for other creatures
config.shadows.creatures.tooltip: Whether the horse, pets and animals from wildlife mods cast shadows.
config.shadows.creaturelength.name: Creature shadow length
config.shadows.creaturelength.tooltip: How long shadows are for the horse, pets, Junimos, critters and wildlife mod animals, compared to everyone else. 1 is unchanged, lower looks better on small animals indoors.
config.shadows.creaturesoftness.name: Creature shadow softness
config.shadows.creaturesoftness.tooltip: How soft those animals' shadows are compared to everyone else. 1 is unchanged, higher blends a small animal's shadow into the floor.
config.shadows.junimolength.name: Junimo shadow length
config.shadows.junimolength.tooltip: Extra length control for Junimo shadows, on top of the creature shadow length. Lower stops a hopping Junimo's face going dark in its own shadow. 1 is unchanged.
config.shadows.contact.name: Dark pool under objects
config.shadows.contact.tooltip: A soft dark spot under objects that cast a shadow, so they look planted on the ground. 0 is off, try 0.5 to 1. Fades with the daylight shadows at dusk and in storms.
config.shadows.contactpeople.name: Dark pool under people
config.shadows.contactpeople.tooltip: A soft dark spot under people and animals so they don't look like they're floating at noon. 0 is off, try 0.5 to 1. Fades with the daylight shadows at dusk.
config.shadows.buildings.tooltip: Barns, coops, sheds, the greenhouse and the farmhouse cast a shadow in their own shape instead of a soft patch underneath. Needs the switch above.
config.shadows.groundforeshortening.name: Ground foreshortening
config.shadows.groundforeshortening.tool: How squashed the shadows of trees, bushes, crops and animals get when they point sideways, to match the game's tilted view. 1 is no squashing. Fences and signs aren't affected, and people have their own setting below.
config.shadows.charactergroundforeshorte: The same squashing for players and NPCs, kept separate so their shadows don't come out too thin. 1 is full width, the usual look. Farm animals use the setting above.
config.shadows.grounded.name: Shadows start at the feet
config.shadows.grounded.tooltip: Keeps a character's shadow attached at the feet and stretching away from the light, by day and under lamps, and lifts it with them when they jump. Off, the shadow swings around the feet, so a lamp beside someone can lay it flat like a fallen person. Replaces the people squashing setting while on.
config.shadows.groundeddepth.name: Footprint depth
config.shadows.groundeddepth.tooltip: For shadows that start at the feet. How thick a body is front to back, so a lamp beside someone leaves a patch under them instead of a thin line. 1 is as thick as the body is wide.
config.shadows.casts.name: Shadows per character
config.shadows.casts.tooltip: How many lights each character casts a shadow from indoors and at night, nearest first. More lights cost more, so in a room full of lamps 1 costs about a third of 3. The sun counts as one light and isn't affected.
config.shadows.perkind.title: Per kind
config.shadows.perkind.tooltip: Shadow length, edge softness and lean for each kind of thing. The Shadow length and Edge softness sliders above scale all of them. A length of 0 turns that kind off completely, which also saves performance (on a farm most shadows are grass tufts).
config.shadows.length.trees.name: Trees
config.shadows.length.smalltrees.name: Saplings & stumps
config.shadows.length.bushes.name: Bushes
config.shadows.length.crops.name: Crops
config.shadows.length.grass.name: Grass
config.shadows.length.objects.name: Forage, fences & machines
config.shadows.length.buildings.name: Barns, sheds & the farmhouse
config.shadows.softness.tooltip: How soft each kind's shadow edge is, as a multiplier on Edge softness above. Short shadows usually want more of it than tall ones.
config.shadows.lean.tooltip: How far each kind's shadow leans compared to the sun's angle. 1 follows the sun and is the default for everything. Lower makes a shadow shorter and more upright, but then it no longer matches the shadows of people nearby.
config.shadows.heightdrop.name: Building & ledge shadows
config.shadows.heightdrop.tooltip: Project ground shadows from walls, buildings, and ledges (requires the Height Framework mod).
config.shadows.heightlength.name: Building shadow length
help.shadowstrength: How dark shadows are. Past 1 they deepen further, soft edges included, up to near black at 3, at no extra cost.
config.camera.mode.name: Camera mode
config.camera.mode.tooltip: Off = the game's own camera, locked on you. Smooth = the view trails a little behind you as you walk and eases back to the middle when you stop, without ever swinging past it.
config.camera.disabled: Smooth camera is switched off for now. With it on, the toolbar could jump between the top and the bottom of the screen while walking diagonally, and it will stay off until that is fixed. Your choice here is kept for when it comes back.
config.mapshot.name: Effects in map screenshots
config.mapshot.tooltip: The game's whole-map screenshot (the camera button in the options, or a mod such as Daily Screenshot) includes this mod's effects, except screen-only ones like the vignette, tilt-shift and drops on the glass. Each shot takes a few seconds longer. Off keeps the game's own picture.
config.smoothcam.speed.name: Follow speed
config.smoothcam.speed.tooltip: Smooth mode only. How far the view trails behind you while you walk. Lower is softer and trails further, 1.0 stays locked on you like the game's camera.
config.renderscale.name: Effect resolution
config.renderscale.tooltip: Resolution of the effects compared to your window. The game itself always stays full size. Lower runs much lighter (0.5 costs about a quarter of 1.0), and 0.5 looks cleanest with pixel art. Values in between can shimmer a bit while the camera moves.
config.sheetupscale.name: Sprites at twice the texels
config.sheetupscale.tooltip: Doubles every sprite with Scale2x so pixel staircases turn into smooth diagonals, without adding new colours. The original art isn't changed. Uses up to 384 MB of video memory and skips very large content-pack sheets.
config.sheetupscalesmoothness.name: Smoothing amount
config.sheetupscalesmoothness.tooltip: 0 keeps the game's own pixels, 1 fully rounds off every staircase corner. It's worked out once, so it costs nothing while you play.
config.sheetupscaleworld.name: The world
config.sheetupscaleworld.tooltip: Terrain, buildings, crops, trees, furniture and every other sprite drawn in the world.
config.sheetupscalecharacters.name: Characters and animals
config.sheetupscalecharacters.tooltip: You, the villagers, monsters and the farm animals.
config.sheetupscaleportraits.name: Portraits
config.sheetupscaleitems.name: Items
config.sheetupscaleitems.tooltip: Tools, weapons, crops, forage, machines, furniture and other items lying in the world. The same items in the toolbar and inventory follow Menus and dialogue.
config.sheetupscaleinterface.name: Menus and dialogue
config.sheetupscaleinterface.tooltip: Menus, the HUD, the dialogue lettering, and the items shown in the toolbar and the inventory. Off keeps the interface exactly as the game drew it.
config.renderscaleauto.name: Lower it automatically when needed
config.renderscaleauto.tooltip: Lowers the effect resolution by itself when the frame rate drops, and raises it again when things calm down. It never goes higher than the slider above. If lowering doesn't help, the slowdown is coming from somewhere else, so it waits before trying again, a little longer each time.
help.renderscaleauto: Drops the effect resolution when frames are slow, and gives it back when they are not. The slider above is the ceiling.
config.lightersofteffects.name: Lighter soft effects
config.lightersofteffects.tooltip: Clouds, bloom, the tilt-shift blur and the lighting are soft by nature, so they can be worked out at a lower resolution with no visible change. When slow does this only while the frame rate is below the game's target, before the effect resolution is lowered. Always keeps it on.
help.lightersofteffects.never: Clouds, bloom, the tilt-shift blur and the lighting are always worked out at full resolution, as before.
help.lightersofteffects.whenslow: When the frame rate drops below the game's target, clouds, bloom, the tilt-shift blur and the lighting are worked out at a lower resolution first, before the effect resolution is lowered. The picture looks the same.
help.lightersofteffects.always: These soft parts are always worked out at a lower resolution. The picture looks the same, and slower graphics cards gain the most.
config.rendersharpness.name: Upscale sharpening
config.rendersharpness.tooltip: How much sharpening is added when the effects are scaled up to your window. 0 is off, 1 is the default (it gets stronger by itself at lower effect resolution), higher is crisper. Does nothing at effect resolution 1.0.
config.limitsamplerslots.name: Skip unusable texture slots
config.limitsamplerslots.tooltip: Skips a check the game does before every draw that is mostly wasted on modern graphics cards. Faster on most PCs and looks exactly the same. Turn it off if the game misbehaves after an update.
help.limitsamplerslots: Skips a wasted check before every draw. It can save about 1.5 ms a frame, and the picture stays the same. Turn it off if something goes wrong.
tuner.desc.looks: Pick a ready-made look, or save your own.
tuner.desc.perf: How much work the effects do. Lower it if the game stutters.
tuner.desc.colorgrade: The overall colour of the picture, its warmth, contrast and richness.
tuner.desc.bloom: Bright things glow and bleed a little light into what is around them.
tuner.desc.lens: Camera-lens touches like blurred edges, darkened corners and colour fringing.
tuner.desc.smoothing: How smooth the Scale2x doubling makes the art, and which art it touches.
tuner.desc.lighting: How dark rooms and nights get, and how lamps pool light.
tuner.desc.windows: Daylight through the glass, the glow after dusk, and the people reflected in it by day.
tuner.desc.shadows: Shadows cast by people, animals and objects, following the sun.
tuner.desc.godrays: Visible shafts of light, from lamps and fires or slanting down from the sun.
tuner.desc.water: Ripples, sparkle and reflections on every water surface.
tuner.desc.cloudshadow: Cloud shadows drifting slowly across the ground outdoors.
tuner.desc.fog: Daytime fog and the thin mist that gathers at night.
tuner.desc.camera: How the camera follows you as you walk.
tuner.desc.debug: Troubleshooting only. Leave this off unless you are reporting a problem.
tuner.perfhud: Show the cost readout on screen
help.perfhud: Shows in the corner how much each part of this mod costs, live as you play, and the top line is the whole game's frame rate, not just this mod. It also warns you when the game window is not focused, since that alone makes the frame rate look much worse.
help.gputime: Adds a second column with the time the graphics card actually spends, which can be much higher than the first column for some effects. Off by default, and it switches itself off if anything goes wrong.
config.debug.name: Debug logging
config.debug.tooltip: Writes extra details to the SMAPI console to help track down problems.
config.report.name: Write a diagnostic report
config.report.tooltip: Saves your version, location, time, weather, settings and installed mods to a file and to the SMAPI log, so you can share it even on a phone. Stand where the problem is before you tick it. It unticks itself right away, which is normal.
help.waterreflectdistort: How much the water bends what it reflects. 0 is a flat mirror, and the water still ripples and sparkles either way.
config.water.reflectdistort.name: Reflection distortion
config.water.reflectdistort.tooltip: How much waves and ripples bend the reflection. 0 is a flat mirror in any look, 1 is the look as designed. The water surface keeps rippling either way.
help.waterreflectbanding: How much the reflection moves in steps when the water ripples. 0 bends smoothly, higher looks more pixel-art but can slice buildings into sliding strips, and 4 is the mod's old look.
config.water.reflectbanding.name: Reflection banding
config.water.reflectbanding.tooltip: How many pixels tall each band of the reflection is when the water ripples. 0 bends smoothly instead of breaking into strips. 4 is the mod's look up to 1.5.6.
help.waterreflectblur: How soft the reflection is. 0 is sharp, 1 is the default, 2 is twice as hazy.
config.water.reflectblur.name: Reflection softness
config.water.reflectblur.tooltip: How much the reflection softens the deeper it goes. 0 is sharp, 1 is the default look, 2 spreads it twice as far. Reflected people and scenery use the same setting.
help.watermodel.modern: The newer water. Ripples move the reflection, it stays still at the shoreline, fades into the water's colour as it gets deeper and shifts with the camera as you walk, with its own sliders below.
help.watermodel.classic: The old water (up to 1.6.1), unchanged, with its three looks and their distortion and banding settings below.
config.water.reflstyle.name: Reflection look
config.water.reflstyle.tooltip: How much the classic water's movement breaks up the reflection. Still keeps it easy to read, Choppy breaks it up and looks deeper. The water keeps rippling either way, and this only applies to the classic water.
config.water.modern.title: The 1.6.2 water
config.water.modern.tooltip: These only work with Water 1.6. While it is on, the classic look, distortion and banding settings above do nothing.
config.water.modernwobble.name: Wobble
config.water.modernwobble.tooltip: How far the ripples move the reflection. 0 keeps it still, 1 moves it about four pixels up and down at most. It never moves right at the water's edge and moves more further out.
help.watermodernwobble: How far the ripples move the reflection. It stays still at the water's edge and moves more further out.
config.water.modernchoppiness.name: Choppiness
config.water.modernchoppiness.tooltip: How many small, quick ripples are added on top of the slow ones. 0 is a calm, glassy pond, 1 is wind-blown water where the reflection shivers.
help.watermodernchoppiness: How rough the surface is. 0 is calm and glassy, 1 is windy.
config.water.modernparallax.name: Parallax
config.water.modernparallax.tooltip: How much the reflection shifts and stretches with the camera as you walk, like a real reflection seen from an angle. 0 is the flat flip of the classic looks.
help.watermodernparallax: How much the reflection shifts as you walk, like real water seen at an angle. 0 is a flat flip.
config.water.modernfresnel.name: Depth fade
config.water.modernfresnel.tooltip: How much the reflection fades into the water's colour as it gets closer to you, and how much its contrast is toned down, like a photo of a lake. 0 keeps the plain bluish tint of the classic looks.
help.watermodernfresnel: How much the reflection fades into the water's colour and how much its contrast is softened.
config.water.modernstretch.name: Vertical stretch
config.water.modernstretch.tooltip: How much longer the reflection is drawn, the way rough water stretches reflections. 1 is no stretch, the same length as the classic water, and the default.
help.watermodernstretch: How much longer the reflection is drawn. 1 is no stretch.
config.water.modernedgesoftness.name: Edge softness
config.water.modernedgesoftness.tooltip: Smooths the jagged edges the ripples leave on reflections along sloped banks, in pixels. 0 is off.
help.watermodernedgesoftness: How much the jagged edges of the reflection are smoothed, in pixels. 0 leaves them sharp.
config.water.modernplungechurn.name: Churn under waterfalls
config.water.modernplungechurn.tooltip: How much the reflection disappears in the foamy water under a waterfall. 0 keeps the reflection right up to the foam.
help.watermodernplungechurn: How much the reflection fades under a waterfall. 0 keeps it right up to the foam.
config.water.modernplungereach.name: Churn reach
config.water.modernplungereach.tooltip: How many tiles below the foot of a waterfall the churn runs before the reflection is back in full.
help.watermodernplungereach: Tiles below the foot of a fall before the mirror is back in full.
config.water.modernlipfade.name: Fade before a waterfall's lip
config.water.modernlipfade.tooltip: How many tiles above the top of a waterfall the stream's reflection fades out, so it does not end in a hard line at the edge. 0 ends it sharp.
help.watermodernlipfade: How many tiles above a waterfall the reflection fades out. 0 ends it sharp at the edge.
help.reflstyle.still: The water still ripples, but the reflection barely moves and is lighter, so you can tell what it shows. Good in rain, when the game makes the water choppier.
help.reflstyle.natural: The reflection moves with the water. This is the mod's usual look.
help.reflstyle.choppy: The water breaks up the reflection and looks deeper. Good for the sea and stormy days.
config.water.model.name: Water
config.water.model.tooltip: Which water to use. Water 1.6 is the newer, more realistic one with its own settings below. Water 1.5 is the old water (up to 1.6.1), unchanged, with its three looks.
config.water.classic.title: The classic water
config.water.classic.tooltip: These apply only while the water is Classic.
tuner.windowcompat: Off: another window mod is drawing its own beam.
//: Plain-language notes shown when the pointer rests on a control in the on-screen tuner.
help.master: Turns every effect in this mod on or off at once. Nothing here touches your save.
help.colorgrade: Changes the colours of the whole picture, like contrast, colour strength and warm or cool light. Off by default, so you see the game's own colours.
help.automood: Lets the colour settings drift with the time of day and the weather instead of staying fixed.
help.contrast: How far apart the darks and brights are. Above 1 makes shadows deeper and highlights brighter, below 1 flattens the picture.
help.saturation: How strong the colours are. 0 is black and white, 1 is unchanged, above 1 is more vivid.
help.temperature: Warm or cool. Right turns the picture orange like late afternoon, left turns it blue like a cloudy day.
help.tonemap: Softens the brightest spots so they do not turn flat white.
help.bluelight: Takes some blue out of the picture, the way a night-time screen filter does. Meant for comfort, not for looks.
help.bloom: Bright things get a soft glow around them, like lights seen through a camera lens.
help.bloomthreshold: How bright a pixel has to be before it starts to glow. Raise it if too much of the screen is glowing.
help.bloomemissiveboost: Coloured lights like lit windows or lava can glow even when they are a bit below the threshold. White and grey never count, so snow does not glow.
help.aurora: On clear winter nights the water reflects slow green and violet curtains of light. You only see them in the water.
help.aurorastrength: How bright the aurora is. 1 is the default, 0 hides it without turning the switch off.
help.snowglint: Snowflakes sparkle in the sun on clear winter days. 0 turns the sparkle off.
help.shootingstars: Now and then on a clear night a shooting star crosses the sky the water reflects. Watch a lake for a minute.
help.shootingstarfrequency: How often a shooting star crosses the night water. 1 is about one a minute, 4 is four times as often.
help.waternightstars: Twinkling starlight on the water after dark. Off still leaves the moonlight and lamp light on the water.
help.waternightstarsamount: How many stars twinkle on the water on a clear night. 1 is the default, 3 fills the water with them.
help.gameweatherplaintint: Makes the game's own rain over water plain grey instead of blue. Only matters when this mod's rain is off.
help.windyspells: Two or three windy spells a day, when trees, rain, leaves, water and clouds all move harder. Off keeps the usual wind.
help.windyspellsstrength: How many times the usual wind a spell blows at its height.
help.shadows: Every character, tree and object casts a shadow of its own shape, leaning away from the sun.
help.shadowmodel.modern: Shadows of placed things start right at the bottom of their art, and horses, pets and animals from wildlife mods cast flat shadows along the ground instead of standing up.
help.shadowmodel.classic: The shadow shapes from up to 1.6, where placed things' shadows float a little off the ground and animals cast upright shadows like people. Only the shape changes, bug fixes stay.
help.shadowlength: How long shadows are, still long at dawn and short at noon. 0 turns this kind of shadow off.
help.goldenhour: Shadows get even longer in the first and last hours of sunlight. Noon is never affected.
help.sunseason: Shadows and day length follow the season, long all day in winter and short at summer noon, with sunrise and sunset shifting too. 0 keeps the same summer sun all year, like before.
help.shadowtint: Gives shadows colour, blue from the sky outdoors, grey in rain, violet when the sun is low and warm indoors. 0 is plain black.
help.shadowblur: How soft shadow edges are, from sharp at 0 to fuzzy like a cloudy day. Softer edges look lighter, so raise shadow strength above 1 to keep them dark.
help.shadowcasts: How many nearby lamps may each throw their own shadow of one character at night. More lamps means more shadows and more work for your machine.
config.shadows.carried.name: Carried lights cast shadows
config.shadows.carried.tooltip: Whether a light you carry, like a glowing ring or a torch, casts shadows of you and people nearby. Off by default, because it puts a dark shadow of you off to one side. It lights the ground either way.
help.shadowcarried: A glowing ring or a torch in hand throws a shadow of you and the people near you. Off, it only lights the ground round you.
help.shadowobjects: Whether trees, fences, crops and furniture cast shadows too, or only people and animals.
help.shadowfences: Whether fences cast shadows, which lay stripes across paths. Off removes only the fence shadows.
help.shadowplayer: Whether your own shadow is drawn, and your co-op partners' with it.
help.shadowvillagers: Whether villagers, monsters and other human-shaped characters cast shadows.
help.shadowfarmanimals: Whether barn and coop animals cast shadows.
help.shadowcreatures: Whether the horse, pets and animals added by wildlife mods cast shadows.
help.shadowgameshadowwhenoff: The player, villagers or animals you switched off above get the game's own round shadow under their feet instead of no shadow.
help.shadowcreaturelength: How long the creatures' shadows are, Junimos and rats included. 1 is as before.
help.shadowcreaturesoftness: How soft the creatures' shadows are, Junimos and rats included. 1 is as before.
help.shadowjunimolength: An extra shadow length just for Junimos, on top of the animal setting. Lower it if a hopping Junimo's face ends up inside its shadow.
help.contactshadow: A soft dark patch under trees, rocks, fences and placed things so they sit on the ground, fading with the daylight shadows at dusk. 0 turns it off, like before 1.7.6.
help.contactshadowpeople: A soft dark patch under every person and animal, which keeps them on the ground at noon when their shadow is short. 0 turns it off, like earlier versions.
help.shadowbuildings: Whether buildings cast shadows in their own shape or just a soft patch underneath. Buildings are the tallest things on the farm, so their shadow length is the first thing to adjust.
help.shadowgroundforeshortening: How flat sideways shadows lie. Lower makes tree and bush shadows hug the ground instead of standing up, and people have their own setting next.
help.shadowcharactergroundforeshortening: How flat a person's sideways shadow lies, separate from trees and objects. Lower makes it thinner at dawn and dusk, 1 is full width.
help.shadowgrounded: Character shadows stay attached at the feet and stretch away from the light, and lift off the ground when they jump. Off, the whole shadow turns around the feet like before.
help.shadowgroundeddepth: How deep the shadow patch under someone's feet is, compared with their width. It's the bit of shadow left under them when a lamp is right beside them.
help.shadowlean: How far shadows stretch away from what casts them. Lower keeps them close to the base instead of stretching out sideways.
help.lighting: Night and indoor lighting. How dark rooms get and how much lamps light them back up.
help.lightindoor: How dark a room is when nothing is lighting it. Higher is darker.
help.lightmorning: How much night darkness is left in the room when you wake up. Raise it for a room that brightens with the sunrise, 0 wakes you to full daylight like the normal game.
help.lightindoorcolour: How much a room's colour changes with the time of day, cool in the morning, warm before dark, blue at night. It doesn't change brightness. 0 keeps the game's own colours.
help.lightmorningcool: How blue a room looks early on a clear morning. Rainy mornings always stay fully blue. 1 is the old look, blue every morning whatever the weather.
help.lightnight: How dark the night is, outdoors and in. Darker nights look cooler and make lamps and fires stand out more.
help.lightwarmth: How orange lamplight is. 0 is white, higher looks more like candlelight.
help.lightboost: How bright each lamp is. Raise this if nights are too dark to get around.
help.lightradius: How wide a pool of light each lamp throws.
help.lightshadows: Whether the light from a lamp is blocked by walls and furniture instead of passing through them.
help.lightsilhouettes: Fences, bushes and boulders block lamp light by their actual shape, so a torch behind a fence shines through the gaps. Off blocks whole tiles with rounder pools of light, like before.
help.lightprops: Kegs, chests, machines, signs and floor furniture block lamp light by their shape. Off, light goes straight through them.
help.floodgi: Bounced light. Light hitting a floor or wall spills onto things nearby, so a lit corner brightens the area around it a little. Often called GI.
help.gimodel.flood: The GI every version has used so far. Light spreads out tile by tile.
help.gimodel.cascades: Newer GI where light travels out and stops at whatever is in the way, so shade and lamp glow follow the shape of things. Needs a graphics card that supports 16-bit colour, otherwise the classic one is used.
help.relief: Gives sprites a lit side and a dark side. A lamp next to a tree lights the half facing it and leaves the other half a bit darker. Bare ground isn't affected.
help.reliefhalfres: Draws the relief at lower resolution and smooths it out. On by default. Off draws it at full size, which costs about four times as much on a big window.
help.reliefstrength: How strong the lit and dark sides from lamps are.
help.reliefsun: How strong the lit and dark sides from the sun are, outdoors in the daytime.
help.reliefrim: A bright fringe on the edge of a sprite facing a lamp, in that lamp's colour. 0 is off.
help.leafshimmer: Canopy patches brighten and dim like leaves flipping in wind. Brightness only, nothing moves. 0 is off.
help.sheetupscale: Doubles the resolution of the game's art so diagonals and curves look smoother, while it still looks like pixel art. Uses more graphics memory.
help.floodstrength: How far bounced light spreads. It changes the difference between lit and unlit parts of a room, not the overall brightness.
help.floodshadow: How dark the areas that bounced light cannot reach become.
help.colourbleed: Bounced light picks up the colour of what it hit, reddish near a red wall, greenish in a field. Only colour changes, not brightness. 0 is off.
help.carriedbounce: A glow ring or torch you carry also adds bounced light to the room. Off, it still lights the ground around you, but the room's bounced light only comes from its own lamps.
help.lightshadowcarve: How much shadows cut into the game's own round lamp glow. 0 leaves the glow whole behind a trunk or fence, 1 cuts the shadow right through it.
help.lightshadowsoftness: How blurry a lamp shadow's edge gets the further it falls from what casts it. 0 is sharp, 1 is the default, 2 is twice as soft.
help.lightshadowdetail: How detailed lamp shadows are. It costs more the more lamps are on screen, so lower this first in busy places. 0 is the fastest.
help.lightshadowshared: Lamps in the same room share shadow detail instead of each doing the full work, which keeps rooms full of lamps running smoothly.
help.lightshadowsharp: Full resolution lamp shadows for the sharpest edges. Off uses half resolution, which saves about a third on a lit street and nearly half in a room full of lamps. Check a keg or fence post next to a lamp to decide.
help.lightshadowcache: Remembers a lamp's shadow while nothing around it moves, instead of redoing it every frame. Free when you stand still and about a tenth of the cost while walking. Off redoes it every frame.
help.wateredsoil: Watered dirt catches the sun and sparkles here and there, gone at night and in rain. 0 is dirt that only darkens.
help.windoweffects: Daylight coming in through windows, the glow on the glass and the light it casts into the room.
help.windowopensnight: A lit window at night pushes back the darkness around it, so the ground in front of the house shows its real colours. 0 leaves the night as it is.
help.lamphalo: A wide faint ring around each real lamp after dark.
help.aquariumripple: A fish tank's light ripples like light through water.
help.tvglow: A TV that is on lights the room like a screen and fades in and out.
help.windowbeam: The visible beam of light on the floor under a window. Turns itself off if another window mod already draws one.
help.windowdetail.wholewindow: The glass, the bars and the frame brighten together, as before. At midday a window with detail in it can turn white.
help.windowdetail.keepdetail: Windows brighten less, so bars, frames and curtains stay visible. Helps windows from texture packs and Alternative Textures. The rest of the room looks the same.
help.windowlightshape.glow: The window glows in a soft oval and the light on the floor is a soft band, as before.
help.windowlightshape.glass: Only the glass glows, so frames and bars stay visible, and the light on the floor keeps the shape of the panes. Works on the game's windows and windows the mod has labels for. Other windows keep the old light.
config.lighting.windowlightshape.name: Window light
config.lighting.windowlightshape.tooltip: As before: the window glows in a soft oval and the light on the floor is a soft band. From the glass: only the glass glows and the light on the floor keeps the shape of the panes.
help.windowglassrays: With From the glass: light hanging in the air below a window, streaking down the way the sun comes in. 0 leaves only the light on the floor.
config.lighting.windowglassrays.name: Window light rays
config.lighting.windowglassrays.tooltip: With Window light set to From the glass: how much light hangs in the air below a window, in streaks falling the way the sun comes in. 0 is none.
help.windowglassraylength: How far the light reaches into the room, the rays and the patch on the floor together. 1 is the length the sun's angle gives.
help.windowglassraywhiteness: How white the rays are. 0 is the colour of the daylight, 1 is plain white.
help.windowglassfloor: How bright the patch of light on the floor is. 0 turns it off.
help.windowglasspane: How bright the glass itself glows. 0 leaves the glass as the game draws it.
help.windowglasscurtaincolour: With From the glass: light through a sheer curtain takes the curtain's colour. Off, the curtain only dims it.
config.lighting.windowglasscurtaincolour: With Window light set to From the glass: light through a sheer curtain takes the curtain's colour. Off, the curtain only dims the light.
help.windowglasscurtainlight: How much light gets through a sheer curtain, compared with clear glass. 0 lets none through, 1 as much as glass.
With Window light set to From the glass: how much light gets through a sheer curtain, compared with clear glass. 0 is none, 1 as much as glass.
help.windowglasscurtaincolourstrength: How deep a colour the light through a curtain takes. 1 is the curtain's own colour, 2 twice as deep, 0 none.
config.lighting.windowglasscurtaincolour: With Curtain colour on: how deep a colour the light through a sheer curtain takes. 1 is the curtain's own colour, 2 twice as deep, 0 none.
config.lighting.windowglassraylength.too: With Window light set to From the glass: how far the light reaches into the room. 1 is the length the sun's angle gives.
With Window light set to From the glass: how white the rays are. 0 is the colour of the daylight.
config.lighting.windowglassfloor.name: Window light on the floor
config.lighting.windowglassfloor.tooltip: With Window light set to From the glass: how bright the patch of light on the floor is. 0 turns it off.
config.lighting.windowglasspane.name: Window glass glow
config.lighting.windowglasspane.tooltip: With Window light set to From the glass: how bright the glass glows. 0 leaves it as the game draws it.
help.windowglassrayspread: How much the beam widens and softens as it falls. 0 keeps the window's shape sharp all the way down.
config.lighting.windowglassrayspread.too: With Window light set to From the glass: how much the beam widens and softens as it falls. 0 keeps the window's shape sharp.
help.windowdaylightstrength: How bright daylight through windows is, including the glass, the beam and the sunlight on the floor. Lower it if windows look blown out white. The room's own light doesn't change.
help.windowdaylightelsewhere: Daylight through windows in every building except your house. Lower it if shops or villagers' homes look blown out. Your farmhouse uses the slider above.
help.windowreflection: People walking past a window show up in the glass, clearly by day and faintly at night once the window is lit inside.
help.windowreflectionindoors: Windows and glass inside buildings reflect the floor and anyone standing in front, clear at night and faint by day. Off reflects outdoors only, like before.
help.godrays: Lamp light streaming past things beside the lamp, like doorways, window frames or a tree by a street lamp. Look at a lit street at night or a fireplace in a dark room. Off by default and needs flood lighting on.
help.cloudshadow: Shadows of clouds drifting across the ground on a sunny day.
help.cloudcoverage: How much of the ground is under a cloud at any moment.
help.stormwarning: The sky closes in through the afternoon when tomorrow brings weather.
help.cloudcount: Few big clouds or many small ones.
help.fog: Drifting mist over the world. Heaviest in the early morning and in the right weather.
help.fognightmist: A separate, thinner mist that comes out after dark.
help.minefogmist: Drifting mist over a foggy mine level, with the torches glowing in it.
help.fognightmistlampglow: Wisps drifting past a lamp light up in its colour. 0 keeps the mist flat.
help.water: Everything the mod does to water, like movement, sparkle and reflections.
help.waterstrength: How strongly the surface moves. Lower it if the ripple is distracting.
help.watersparkle: The glints of light on the surface.
help.watersparkleday: The glints on the water while the sun is up.
help.watersparklenight: The glints on the water after dusk. Fades in and out with the evening.
help.watercaustics: The wavy pattern of light on the bottom of shallow water.
help.watersparklecloud: A cloud shadow passing over the water takes the sun's glitter with it.
help.waterreflection: Water reflects what's next to it. Only things on screen can be reflected, so something far above the top of the screen won't show yet.
help.waterindoors: Whether indoor water, such as a tub or a fish tank, gets the effect too.
help.tiltshift: Blurs the top and bottom of the screen and keeps the middle sharp, which makes the world look like a small model. Turn it off for an evenly sharp picture.
help.tiltfeather: How gradually the blur comes on at the edge of the sharp area.
help.tilttop: How much of the top of the screen is blurred.
help.tiltbottom: How much of the bottom of the screen is blurred.
help.tiltindoor: How much blur is kept indoors, since rooms are only a few tiles deep. 0 keeps rooms fully sharp.
help.vignette: Darkens the corners of the screen like a camera lens, drawing the eye to the middle.
help.ca: Splits colours slightly apart towards the corners of the screen, like a real lens. The middle stays clean.
config.godrays.sun.name: Sun shafts
config.godrays.sun.tooltip: Sunlight through gaps in the trees, as bright patches on the ground rather than beams in the air. It leans with the time of day, gets hazier in fog and goes away when it's overcast. Shows best in forests and along treelines, and doesn't need the lamp shafts switch.
help.godrayssun: Sunlight through gaps in the trees, as patches on the ground rather than beams in the air, leaning with the time of day. Look at a forest floor or a treeline. Doesn't need the lamp switch.
config.particles.enabled.name: Enable particles
config.particles.enabled.tooltip: Small things floating in the world, like blossom on the wind, dust in sunlight and sparks over a fire. They're lit and coloured like everything else on the map. Off by default, since it adds things the game never had.
config.particles.density.name: How many, overall
config.particles.density.tooltip: Overall amount for every kind at once. Each kind below has its own amount on top of this. Lower this first if the frame rate drops.
tuner.desc.particles: Blossom, dust and sparks drifting through the world
help.particles: Small things floating in the world, like petals on the wind, dust in sunlight and sparks over a fire. They're lit and coloured along with everything else.
help.particledensity: Overall amount for every kind at once. Each kind below has its own amount on top of this. Lower this first if the frame rate drops.
help.particleoldnightshade: 0 lets leaves and petals in the air outdoors darken at night just like the ground under them. 1 is the darker look from before, where leaves could turn almost black at night.
config.particles.dust.name: Dust in the daylight
config.particles.dust.tooltip: Dust specks floating in the light from a window. Indoors only, while sunlight is actually coming in.
help.particledust: Dust floating in window light indoors, while the window is lit. Try your farmhouse in the morning and look at the light on the floor.
config.particles.amount.name: How much
config.particles.amount.tooltip: How much of this kind there is. It stacks with the overall amount above, so that slider still turns everything down. 0 works like off but fades out instead of stopping.
config.particles.size.name: How big
config.particles.size.tooltip: How big each piece is compared with normal.
help.particleamount: How much of this one there is. The overall amount at the top of the tab still turns everything down at once.
help.particlesize: How big one piece of it is.
config.particles.embers.name: Sparks over a fire
config.particles.embers.tooltip: Sparks rising off fires like hearths, braziers, torches and wall sconces. They glow on their own and fade out in daylight when outdoors.
help.particleembers: Sparks rising off a hearth, a brazier or a torch. Stand by the saloon fireplace after dark. Outdoors they fade into daylight the way lamps do.
config.particles.fireflies.name: Fireflies
config.particles.fireflies.tooltip: Extra fireflies over fields on summer nights, on top of the game's own. They come out on the same nights the game's do.
help.particlefireflies: Fireflies over a field on a summer night, added to the ones the game already flies. Stand outdoors in summer after dark.
config.particles.petals.name: Blossom and leaves
config.particles.petals.tooltip: Petals drift outdoors in spring and leaves in summer and autumn, even on days the game has nothing in the air. On the game's windy days it thins out and follows that wind, and there are none in winter or rain.
help.particlepetals: Petals in spring, leaves in summer and autumn, drifting outdoors even when the game has nothing in the air. Thins out on the game's own windy days.
config.particles.petalsflutter.name: Flutter
config.particles.petalsflutter.tooltip: How much falling leaves and petals bend as they tumble. It changes their shape, not where they go. 0 falls flat.
config.particles.leaflook.name: Leaf look
config.particles.leaflook.tooltip: Realistic: smooth petals and leaves that bend as they fall. Pixel: the game's own leaf art, flipping over the way it does on windy days, and drawn from a recolour mod's art if you use one.
config.particles.tumbleweeds.name: Tumbleweeds
config.particles.tumbleweeds.tooltip: Now and then a tumbleweed rolls across the desert with the wind, bouncing over the sand.
config.particles.whirlwinds.name: Whirlwinds
config.particles.whirlwinds.tooltip: In a storm or on a windy day, now and then a small whirlwind of leaves and dust wanders across the ground.
config.particles.whirlwindleaves.name: Leaves in a whirlwind
config.particles.whirlwindleaves.tooltip: How many leaves a whirlwind picks up. 0 is dust only, 2 is twice the usual leaves.
help.particlepetalsflutter: How much a leaf or petal buckles as it falls. It bends the shape, not the path. 0 is a flat fall.
help.particleleaflook.realistic: Smooth petals and leaves that bend as they fall.
help.particleleaflook.pixel: Petals and leaves from the game's own art, flipping over the way the game's leaves do.
help.particletumbleweeds: Now and then a tumbleweed rolls across the desert with the wind.
help.particlewhirlwinds: In storms and on windy days, a small whirlwind of leaves and dust now and then spins across the ground.
help.particlewhirlwindleaves: How many leaves a whirlwind picks up. 0 is dust only.
config.particles.ringsparkles.name: Sparks around a glow ring
config.particles.ringsparkles.tooltip: Pale sparks circling you while you wear a glow ring. They stay where they appear, so they circle you when you stand still and trail behind when you walk.
config.particles.footdust.name: Dust under your feet
config.particles.footdust.tooltip: Anyone crossing dry dirt or sand kicks up a little dust, villagers included. Stone, grass and wood lift nothing, and neither does wet ground.
config.particles.glowlight.name: Glowing particles cast light
config.particles.glowlight.tooltip: Groups of embers, fireflies or lava sparks light up what is around them in their own colour. The more there are, the brighter it gets. 0 turns it off.
config.particles.chimney.name: Chimneys throw sparks
config.particles.chimney.tooltip: Heat shimmers over chimneys, and after dark a few sparks rise with the smoke. Only buildings with a chimney get it.
config.particles.festivelights.name: The winter tree twinkles
config.particles.festivelights.tooltip: Each bulb on the town's winter tree blinks in its own colour instead of glowing warm white. Off keeps them warm white.
help.particleringsparkles: Pale sparks circling you while you wear a glow ring. Stand still, then walk, and they trail behind instead of following.
help.particlefootdust: Dry dirt and sand lift dust when somebody walks over them.
help.particlechimney: Heat over a chimney, and sparks in the smoke after dark.
help.particlefestivelights: The town tree's bulbs wink in colour rather than glowing white.
help.particleglowlight: Gathered embers and fireflies light what is around them.
config.particles.waterfallmist.name: Mist at a waterfall
config.particles.waterfallmist.tooltip: Spray rising where a waterfall lands, including waterfalls added by other mods. Beach waves get none.
config.particles.waterfallrainbowsun.nam: Rainbow only under a low sun
config.particles.waterfallrainbowsun.too: Only show the waterfall rainbow when the sun is low enough, so none around a summer midday and all day in winter. Off shows it whenever the sun is out.
config.particles.waterfallrainbow.name: Rainbow in the spray
config.particles.waterfallrainbow.toolti: A rainbow in the waterfall spray while the sun is out, fading in rain and after dark. It needs the waterfall mist switch on, and 0 is none.
help.particlewaterfallmist: Spray hanging at the foot of a fall. The mountain lake's waterfall is the nearest one to a farm.
help.waterfallrainbowsun: The rainbow needs a low sun, so none around a summer midday and all day in winter. Off shows it whenever the sun is out.
help.waterfallrainbow: A rainbow in the spray at the foot of a fall while the sun is out. 0 is none.
config.particles.hotspringsteam.name: Steam over hot water
config.particles.hotspringsteam.tooltip: Slow steam rising off hot water, like the bathhouse pool or hot springs from mods that support it.
help.particlehotspringsteam: Wisps over the bathhouse pool and other hot water. Stand in the bathhouse to see it.
config.particles.lavasparks.name: Sparks off lava
config.particles.lavasparks.tooltip: Hot sparks popping off lava and dying out before they land. You will see them in the volcano and on the lava floors of the mines.
help.particlelavasparks: Sparks over molten rock. The volcano and mine floors 80 to 119 are where to look.
config.godrays.sunintensity.name: Sun shaft strength
config.godrays.sunintensity.tooltip: How strong the sunlight coming through the trees is. This is separate from the lamp rays slider.
config.godrays.sunreach.name: Sun shaft reach
config.godrays.sunreach.tooltip: How far the patches of sunlight stretch out from the trees. Higher reaches further into open ground.
help.godrayssunintensity: How strong the sunlight coming through the trees is. Separate from the lamp rays slider.
help.godrayssunreach: How far the dappled patches stretch from the trees that cut them. Higher reaches further into the open ground.
config.godrays.sunglassroof.name: Sun through a glass roof
config.godrays.sunglassroof.tooltip: Dappled sunlight on the floor of glass-roofed rooms like the greenhouse. Turning it off does not affect the sun shafts outdoors.
help.godrayssunglassroof: Dappled sunlight on the floor of glass-roofed rooms like the greenhouse. Turning it off leaves the sun shafts outdoors alone.
tuner.desc.weather: Rain and snow drawn by this mod instead of the game. Rain leans with the wind and splashes, and snow falls as real flakes.
config.precipitation.enabled.name: Radiance rain & snow
config.precipitation.enabled.tooltip: Let this mod draw rain and snow instead of the game. Rain leans with the wind and splashes, and snow falls as flakes. Off keeps the game's own rain and snow.
config.weather.foliagesway.name: Wind in the trees
config.weather.foliagesway.tooltip: Trees and bushes sway gently in the wind, moving at the top while the trunk stays put. Storms push them further.
config.weather.foliageswaystrength.name: How far the crowns lean
config.weather.foliageswaystrength.toolt: How far trees lean at the peak of a gust. 1 moves a grown tree's top about two pixels on a calm day, 2 doubles that, and 0 is still.
config.weather.foliageswayspeed.name: Tempo
config.weather.foliageswayspeed.tooltip: How fast the trees sway. 1 is a big tree's natural pace. Storms make them lean further, not faster.
config.weather.foliageswaygustspan.name: Gust length (tiles)
config.weather.foliageswaygustspan.toolt: How wide one gust is, in tiles. Short gusts make trees next to each other move differently, and long ones roll down a whole row.
config.weather.foliageswaycrops.name: Crops lean with the wind
config.weather.foliageswaycrops.tooltip: Grown crops sway in the same wind as the trees, and more than trees do since they are short. Seeds and sprouts stay still.
config.weather.foliageswaygrass.name: Grass sways with the wind
config.weather.foliageswaygrass.tooltip: Grass sways in the same wind as the trees, each blade on its own, so gusts roll through a meadow in waves.
config.weather.grasssmoothshake.name: Grass settles smoothly
config.weather.grasssmoothshake.tooltip: Grass you walk through or cut swings like a spring and settles smoothly, instead of the game's jerky shake that can snap upright. Running still shakes it more than walking.
config.precipitation.rain.name: Replace rain
