config.precipitation.rain.tooltip: Replace the rain, green rain included.
config.precipitation.snow.name: Replace snow
config.precipitation.density.name: Amount
config.precipitation.density.tooltip: How much falls, compared to the weather's normal amount.
help.precipitation: Let this mod draw rain and snow instead of the game. Rain leans with the wind and splashes, snow falls as flakes, and storms rain harder.
help.foliagesway: Trees and bushes sway in the wind, moving at the top while the trunk stays put. Storms push them further.
help.foliageswaystrength: How far trees lean at the peak of a gust. 1 moves a grown tree's top about two pixels on a calm day.
help.foliageswaycrops: Grown crops lean in the gust as the trees do.
help.foliageswaygrass: Grass leans in the gust blade by blade, so the wind runs through a meadow.
help.grasssmoothshake: Grass you walk through swings like a spring and settles, instead of the game's zigzag that can snap upright.
help.precipitationrain: Replace the rain. Green rain gets replaced too.
help.precipitationsnow: Replace the snow with drifting flakes in three sizes.
help.precipitationdensity: How much falls, compared to the weather's normal amount.
config.lightning.name: Lightning response
config.lightning.tooltip: Lightning strikes light up the scene for a moment. Shadows flick toward the bolt and a short warm glow follows. If the game's screen flash option is off, only a softer version stays.
help.lightning: After each strike, shadows flick toward the bolt for a moment and a short warm glow follows. Works with the game's own rain too.
config.wetworld.lensdrops.name: Drops on the screen edge
config.wetworld.lensdrops.tooltip: A few drops cling to the screen edges while it rains, and frost while it snows. They never cover the middle and clear up soon after the weather stops.
help.wetworldlensdrops: A few drops on the edges of the screen while it rains, frost while it snows. Never the middle of the picture.
config.lightningbolts.name: Visible bolts
config.lightningbolts.tooltip: Show lightning bolts in the sky on every map, using the game's own art. Normally the game only shows one on the farm when something gets hit.
help.lightningbolts: A bolt in the sky with the flash on any map, using the game's own art. Some strikes stay hidden behind the clouds.
config.lightningwindows.name: Lightning through windows
config.lightningwindows.tooltip: Indoors during a storm, lightning flashes through the windows and lights the room for a moment. The game itself only flashes outdoors.
help.lightningwindows: Indoors during a storm, the windows flash white with lightning and throw that light into the room for a moment.
config.precipitation.wind.name: Replace windblown leaves
config.precipitation.wind.tooltip: Replace the windy-day debris with blossom in spring, leaves in summer and autumn and white flecks in winter. They tumble along with the wind at different depths.
help.precipitationwind: On windy days, swaps the flat bits the game blows across the screen for blossoms or leaves that tumble on the same wind as the rain, in three layers of depth and coloured for the season where you are. Uses the leaf look below, the same setting as in the Particles tab.
config.precipitation.size.name: Size
config.precipitation.size.tooltip: How big each piece is, compared to normal.
config.precipitation.opacity.name: Visibility
config.precipitation.opacity.tooltip: How visible it is, separate from how much there is.
help.precipitationsize: How big each piece is, compared to normal.
help.precipitationopacity: How strongly it shows, apart from how much of it there is.
config.precipitation.stormdensity.name: Storm is heavier than rain
config.precipitation.stormdensity.toolti: How much more rain falls in a thunderstorm than in normal rain, building up over a few seconds as the storm comes in. 1 makes a storm look like plain rain.
help.precipitationstormdensity: How much more rain falls in a thunderstorm than in plain rain. 1 is the same as rain.
config.precipitation.rainslant.name: Rain slant
config.precipitation.rainslant.tooltip: How hard the rain slants with the wind. 1 follows the game's wind and 0 falls straight down. Above 1 the rain slants even on a calm day.
help.precipitationrainslant: How hard the rain slants. Above 1 it slants even on a calm day, and 0 falls straight down.
config.precipitation.windslant.name: How steeply petals fall
config.precipitation.windslant.tooltip: How steeply wind-blown petals and leaves fall. Higher falls more steeply, lower drifts flatter across the screen. 1 is the default.
help.precipitationwindslant: How steeply wind-blown petals and leaves come down. Lower streaks them flat across the screen, higher drops them more steeply.
config.wetworld.lensdropsize.name: Drop size
config.wetworld.lensdropsize.tooltip: How big the drops on the glass are, compared to normal.
config.wetworld.edgehaze.name: Misted edge
config.wetworld.edgehaze.tooltip: Fog along the screen edges when it rains, and frost creeping in from the corners when it snows. 0 leaves the glass clear around the drops.
config.wetworld.lensdropliveliness.name: Lively drops
config.wetworld.lensdropliveliness.toolt: How lively the drops on the glass are. Higher makes drops come and go faster and run down the sides more often. 0 keeps them as before.
config.wetworld.lensdropsrefract.name: Drops bend the picture
config.wetworld.lensdropsrefract.tooltip: Each drop on the glass acts like a tiny lens, showing the world behind it upside down, like rain on a camera. Off keeps the drops as before.
config.wetworld.lensdroplook.name: Lens look
config.wetworld.lensdroplook.tooltip: Which lens the drops use when they bend the picture. The 2.2.7 lens is soft, and the 2.3.1 lens shows a sharp, smaller picture in each drop with a darker rim and a brighter glint.
config.wetworld.lensdropspread.name: Drops across the screen
config.wetworld.lensdropspread.tooltip: Adds small drops across the whole screen, not just the edges, up to about seventy. 0 keeps the drops on the edges only.
help.wetworldlensdropsize: How big the drops on the glass are, compared to normal.
help.wetworldedgehaze: Fog along the screen edges in rain, frost creeping in from the corners in snow. 0 leaves the glass clear around the drops.
help.wetworldlensdropliveliness: Drops appear and fade faster, trickles run more often and big drops slide down the edges. 0 keeps the old drops.
help.wetworldlensdropsrefract: Each drop acts like a tiny lens and shows the world behind it upside down and smaller. Off keeps the old drops.
help.lensdroplook.plain: Beads of water on the glass that do not bend the picture behind them.
help.lensdroplook.lens227: Each drop bends the picture like a soft lens. Same look as in 2.2.7.
help.lensdroplook.lens231: Each drop shows a small, sharp, upside-down picture with a dark rim and a bright glint. Looks like water even on a wide screen.
help.wetworldlensdropspread: Small drops all over the screen, not just at the edges. 0 keeps them at the edges only.
help.cloudscale: How big each cloud shadow is. Bigger means fewer, wider patches of shade.
help.fogscale: How big each patch of mist is. Bigger means wider, slower shapes.
help.fogmorningonly: Day fog only in the morning, thickest at dawn and clearing slowly. Off keeps it all day.
help.fogmorninglifthour: The time the morning fog is fully gone. It fades out over the 90 minutes before that.
config.fog.topbias.name: Thicker toward the top
config.fog.topbias.tooltip: How much thicker the fog is at the top of the screen than at the bottom, so it looks further away. 0 is even, 1 is twice as thick at the top. Affects both day fog and night mist.
help.fogtopbias: How much thicker the fog is at the top of the screen, so it looks further away. 0 is even, 1 is twice as thick. Affects day fog and night mist.
config.heathaze.name: Heat haze
config.heathaze.tooltip: Hot air over lava, chimneys and the blacksmith's forge makes the picture shimmer, like air over a road in summer. It fades out around your character so you stay sharp. Hot springs steam instead.
config.heathaze.strength.name: How far it bends
config.heathaze.strength.tooltip: How strong the shimmer is. 1 moves the picture about a pixel and a half where the air is hottest, 0 is off.
help.heathaze: Hot air over lava, chimneys and the blacksmith's forge bends the picture. The volcano and Clint's shop are where to look.
help.heathazestrength: How strong the shimmer is where the air is hottest.
config.water.rainringdensity.name: How many rings
config.water.rainringdensity.tooltip: How many raindrops hit the water, compared to the game's own rain. Below 1 is fewer, above 1 is more. 0 keeps the water smooth in the rain.
config.water.rainringsize.name: Ring size
config.water.rainringsize.tooltip: How wide each ring grows before it fades. Bigger rings also get thicker so they still look like water.
config.water.rainringstrength.name: How visible they are
config.water.rainringstrength.tooltip: How bright the rain rings and splashes are on the water. This doesn't change how many there are or how big they get.
config.water.wakerings.name: Rings from things in the water
config.water.wakerings.tooltip: Rings from anything in the water, like you wading, an NPC crossing, a duck or your fishing float. 0 keeps the water still like before.
help.waterrainringdensity: How many raindrops hit the water. 0 keeps it smooth in the rain, above 1 is busier.
help.waterrainringsize: How wide each ring grows before it fades.
help.waterrainringstrength: How bright the rings are. Doesn't change how many or how big.
tuner.waterwakerings: Rings from things in the water
help.waterwakerings: Rings from anything in the water, like you wading, a duck or your fishing float. 0 keeps the water still.
help.waterfishspot: Fishing spots with bubbles also stir the water around them. 0 keeps them as still as the rest.
config.water.fishspotrings.name: Fish stir a bubbling spot
config.water.fishspotrings.tooltip: Fishing spots with bubbles keep making small rings, faster and stronger during a fish frenzy. Works together with Rings from things in the water. 0 keeps the spot as still as the rest of the water.
config.water.wind.name: Wind moves the water
config.water.wind.tooltip: The wind that tilts the rain and bends the trees also moves the water. Ripples drift with it, gusts ruffle across lakes and there is more sparkle while it blows. 0 keeps the water windless like before.
config.water.riverflow.name: Rivers flow
config.water.riverflow.tooltip: Rivers on maps with a waterfall flow downstream, taking their ripples, sparkle and foam with them. Off keeps rivers still like before. The speed, rain and foam settings only work while this is on.
config.water.current.name: River current speed
config.water.current.tooltip: How fast rivers flow. Only maps with a waterfall get a flowing river, and it follows the bends and runs a bit faster through narrow parts. 0 keeps the old still water.
config.water.rainswell.name: Rain swells the river
config.water.rainswell.tooltip: Rivers flow faster in bad weather. At 1 they run 1.4 times as fast in rain and 1.8 times in a storm, and snow doesn't count. 0 keeps the same speed in any weather.
config.water.riverfoam.name: Foam on the river
config.water.riverfoam.tooltip: Little bits of foam floating with the current, so you can see which way the river flows. Thickest under waterfalls. 0 turns it off.
config.water.seawaves.name: Sea wave strength
config.water.seawaves.tooltip: How strongly the sea moves on the beach, Ginger Island and other coasts, on top of the main wave setting. Rivers, ponds and lakes aren't affected. 1 is the normal sea.
config.water.searainswell.name: Sea swell in rain
config.water.searainswell.tooltip: How much rougher the sea gets in rain, and rougher still in a storm. Rivers, ponds and lakes aren't affected. 0 keeps the sea the same.
help.waterriverflow: Rivers flow downstream from the waterfall. Off keeps them still like before.
help.watercurrent: How fast rivers flow from the waterfall to the edge of the map. Maps without a waterfall don't change. 0 is the old still water.
help.waterrainswell: Rivers run faster in rain and faster again in a storm. 0 keeps one speed.
help.waterriverfoam: Bits of foam floating with the current, thickest under waterfalls. 0 turns it off.
help.waterseawaves: How strongly the sea moves on the coasts, on top of the main wave setting. Rivers and ponds aren't affected. 1 is the normal sea.
help.watersearainswell: The sea gets rougher in rain and rougher still in a storm. Rivers and ponds aren't affected. 0 keeps the sea the same.
config.water.riverripplespeed.name: River ripple speed
config.water.riverripplespeed.tooltip: How much faster the small ripples, sparkle and foam move than the river itself, while big ripples lag behind. This keeps the water from looking thick. 1 moves everything at one speed.
help.waterriverripplespeed: How much faster the small ripples and glints run than the river. 1 moves everything together.
config.water.riverrenew.name: River surface renewal
config.water.riverrenew.tooltip: How often the river's surface pattern changes, so it breaks up and reforms like real water instead of sliding along like syrup. 0 keeps one pattern sliding.
help.waterriverrenew: How often the river's surface pattern changes instead of just sliding along. 0 keeps one pattern.
config.water.riverbankdrag.name: River slower at the banks
config.water.riverbankdrag.tooltip: How much slower the river flows near the banks than in the middle. 0 is the same speed all the way across.
help.waterriverbankdrag: How much slower the river runs along its banks than mid-stream. 0 is one pace bank to bank.
config.water.riverswirl.name: River swirl
config.water.riverswirl.tooltip: How much the current wanders and swirls instead of flowing in straight lines. 0 follows the river exactly.
help.waterriverswirl: How far the current wanders and eddies. 0 follows the river's course exactly.
config.water.riverglitter.name: River glints flash
config.water.riverglitter.tooltip: How the sun sparkles on a river. 0 twinkles steadily like still water, higher gives quick bright flashes like moving water.
help.waterriverglitter: 0 twinkles steadily like still water, higher gives the river quick short flashes.
config.water.riverfoamstreak.name: River foam streaks
config.water.riverfoamstreak.tooltip: How much the river foam stretches along the current. Low is round dots, high is long streaks. 1.8 is the original look.
help.waterriverfoamstreak: How far the river's foam is drawn out along the current. 1.8 is how it first looked.
config.water.riverwaves.name: River wavelets
config.water.riverwaves.tooltip: Small broken rows of waves riding the current, with white tips. Calmer where the river is slow. 0 turns them off.
help.waterriverwaves: Small waves riding the current with white on their crests. 0 draws none.
config.water.riverpixelstep.name: River moves in pixel steps
config.water.riverpixelstep.tooltip: Moves the river surface in pixel steps, twelve a second like the game's own water, instead of gliding smoothly. Some players think smooth motion looks like jelly under pixel art, others prefer it.
help.waterriverpixelstep: Move the river's surface in pixel steps, twelve a second, like the game's own water, instead of gliding.
help.waterwind: The wind that tilts the rain and bends the trees also moves the water. Ripples drift with it and there is more sparkle while it blows. 0 keeps the water windless.
help.wetworld: Rain makes the ground dark and shiny depending on the surface, puddles form on paths and dirt, and lamps leave long streaks on the wet ground at night.
help.wetworldstrength: How dark and glossy the ground gets. Dirt and stone darken most, grass less, wood hardly at all.
help.wetworldpuddles: How much standing water collects on paths and dirt, 0 for none. Puddles fill while it rains and shrink from the edges after.
help.wetpuddlelook.realistic: Smooth puddle edges and lamp streaks, with rain rings like the river's.
help.wetpuddlelook.pixel: Puddle edges, rain rings and lamp streaks in whole pixels, like the game's own art.
config.wetworld.puddlelook.name: Puddle look
config.wetworld.puddlelook.tooltip: Realistic: smooth edges and rain rings like the river's. Pixel: edges, rings and streaks in whole pixels.
help.wetworldpuddlereflection: How clearly people and things next to a puddle reflect in it.
help.wetworldlightstreaks: How bright lamp streaks are on wet ground at night. They get longer and more broken in heavy rain.
help.wetworldlightstreaklength: How long lamp streaks on wet ground are, as a multiple of their normal length.
help.wetworldlightstreakangle: Which way lamp streaks lean. 0 points straight at you, negative leans left and positive leans right.
help.wetworldlightstreakglow: How much soft light spreads round each lamp streak on the wet ground. 0 is a bare line.
help.wetworldlightstreakstone: How much lamp streaks light up the tops of stones and leave the gaps between them dark. 0 is a smooth, even streak.
help.wetworldlightstreakripples: How much rain breaks lamp streaks into short, twinkling sideways dashes. 0 keeps one solid streak.
help.wetworldlightstreakwarmth: How orange white lamps look on wet ground, like sodium street lights. Coloured lights keep their colour, and 0 uses the game's own colour.
help.wetworldlightstreaktaper: How much lamp streaks start as a bright spot at the lamp's base and widen as they stretch away. 0 keeps the same width all the way.
help.wetworldlightpool: How bright the wet shine is on the ground around the foot of a lamp.
help.wetworlddrylamplight: On a dry night, lamps still leave a faint streak and pool of light on stone and paths. How strong, compared with a wet night. 0 turns it off.
config.wetworld.enabled.name: Wet ground in the rain
config.wetworld.enabled.tooltip: Rain darkens the ground and makes it shine, most on dirt and stone, less on grass and barely on wood. Puddles form on paths and dirt away from buildings, fences and grass, and lamps leave long coloured streaks at night. Off by default.
config.wetworld.strength.name: How wet
config.wetworld.strength.tooltip: How dark and glossy wet ground gets.
config.wetworld.puddles.name: Puddles
config.wetworld.puddles.tooltip: How much standing water collects on paths and dirt, 0 for none. Puddles fill while it rains, stay a while after the ground dries, then shrink from the edges. Off when Dynamic Reflections is installed, which has its own puddles.
config.wetworld.puddlereflection.name: Puddle reflections
config.wetworld.puddlereflection.tooltip: How clearly people and things next to a puddle reflect in it.
config.wetworld.lightstreaks.name: Lamp streaks
config.wetworld.lightstreaks.tooltip: How bright the streaks from lamps and lit windows are on wet ground at night. They point toward you, look sharper across puddles and get longer and more broken in heavy rain.
config.wetworld.lightstreaklength.name: Streak length
config.wetworld.lightstreaklength.toolti: How long lamp streaks on wet ground are, as a multiple of their normal length.
config.wetworld.lightstreakangle.name: Streak angle
config.wetworld.lightstreakangle.tooltip: Which way lamp streaks lean, in degrees. 0 points straight at you, negative leans left and positive leans right.
config.wetworld.lightstreakglow.name: Streak glow
config.wetworld.lightstreakglow.tooltip: How much soft light spreads round each lamp streak on the wet ground. 0 is a bare line.
config.wetworld.lightstreakstone.name: Streak on the stones
config.wetworld.lightstreakstone.tooltip: How much lamp streaks light up the tops of stones and leave the gaps between them dark. 0 is a smooth, even streak.
config.wetworld.lightstreakripples.name: Streak ripples
config.wetworld.lightstreakripples.toolt: How much rain breaks lamp streaks into short, twinkling sideways dashes. 0 keeps one solid streak.
config.wetworld.lightstreakwarmth.name: Streak warmth
config.wetworld.lightstreakwarmth.toolti: How orange white lamps look on wet ground, like sodium street lights. Coloured lights keep their colour, and 0 uses the game's own colour.
config.wetworld.lightstreaktaper.name: Streak shape
config.wetworld.lightstreaktaper.tooltip: How much lamp streaks start as a bright spot at the lamp's base and widen as they stretch away. 0 keeps the same width all the way.
config.wetworld.lightpool.name: Light pool
config.wetworld.lightpool.tooltip: How bright the wet shine is on the ground around the foot of a lamp.
config.wetworld.drylamplight.name: Lamps on dry ground
config.wetworld.drylamplight.tooltip: On a dry night, lamps still leave a faint streak and pool of light on stone and paths. How strong, compared with a wet night. 0 turns it off.
config.water.reflectdepth.name: Reflection depth
config.water.reflectdepth.tooltip: How far reflections reach into the water before fading to sky. Higher suits big lakes, lower suits narrow streams where the reflection runs past the far bank. 1 is the default, about 0.55 matches 1.5.3.
config.water.reflectreach.name: Reflection reach
config.water.reflectreach.tooltip: How much of the scene shows up in reflections. Lower it and things far from the water stop reflecting. This is the cheapest way to save performance without turning reflections off.
help.reflectdepth: How far reflections reach into the water before fading to sky. Lower it if reflections in narrow streams run past the far bank.
help.reflectreach: How much of the scene reflects at all. Lower costs less and mirrors fewer things.
config.zoomareafilter.name: Sharp zoom
config.zoomareafilter.tooltip: Keeps edges sharp and steady when your zoom isn't 100 percent. Without it thin lines shimmer at 75 percent and the art gets blurry above 100 percent. Works with Smooth art on or off.
config.sheetupscalestyle.name: Smoothing look
config.sheetupscalestyle.tooltip: Scale2x (1.7) doubles the art and rounds the corners but keeps pixel edges. Soft 4x (1.7.5) redraws it four times larger with smooth curves, like a texture upscaler mod. Soft 4x uses a lot of memory, so only small sheets like items, furniture, characters and portraits get it and big ones stay at 2x.
config.sheetupscalekernel.name: Soft 4x rule
config.sheetupscalekernel.tooltip: Which rule makes the Soft 4x art. xBR (1.7.5) is the softest. MMPX is made for pixel art and keeps lines whole using only the art's own colours. MMPX, edges kept is the same but leaves sprite outlines alone. EPX is the 1.7 rule done twice, the sharpest. None of them cost anything while you play.
help.sheetupscalekernel.xbr: Rounds diagonals and curves with soft edges. The soft look since 1.7.5.
help.sheetupscalekernel.mmpx: Made for pixel art. Keeps thin lines and curves whole and adds no new colours. Sharper than xBR.
help.sheetupscalekernel.mmpxedgeguarded: Like MMPX, but it doesn't round a sprite's outline out into the empty space around it.
help.sheetupscalekernel.epx: The 1.7 rule done twice. The sharpest and closest to the original pixels, with only stair-step corners rounded.
config.sheetupscalekernelfamily.name: Rule
config.sheetupscalekernelfamily.tooltip: Soft 4x only. Picks the rule for this kind of art. Same as all uses the rule chosen above, or pick another just for this group, like xBR for characters and MMPX for the world. Click to cycle through the choices.
config.sheetupscalegradients.name: Smooth gradients
config.sheetupscalegradients.tooltip: Soft 4x only. Smooths the colour bands in things like skies and lit walls into soft gradients, while keeping outlines and real edges sharp. 0 keeps the bands.
config.sheetupscalesteady.name: Steady while moving
config.sheetupscalesteady.tooltip: Soft 4x only. 0 is the sharpest. Higher stops thin lines from shimmering when the camera moves or trees sway, but softens the picture a little. Barely costs anything.
help.sheetupscalestyle.scale2x: Doubles the art and rounds the corners, edges stay pixel edges. The 1.7 look.
help.sheetupscalestyle.soft4x: Redraws the art four times larger with smooth curves, like a texture upscaler mod. Small sheets only, big ones stay at 2x.
config.shadows.sunbearing.name: Sun direction
config.shadows.sunbearing.tooltip: Which side of the screen the sun is on, in degrees. 0 puts it below the screen so shadows fall away from you, which is the default. 180 puts it behind and shadows fall toward you. Shadows still move through the day around this.
help.shadowsunbearing: Drag the dial to move the sun. The warm-coloured mark is the sun and the dark line shows where shadows fall. Shadows still move through the day around where you set noon.
config.shadows.sunlightbearing.name: Sun direction for the light
config.shadows.sunlightbearing.tooltip: Which side the sun is on for light, like sunbeams through trees, the lit side of sprites, window light and sparkle on water. It uses the same numbers as Sun direction, so set them equal to make light and shadows match. By default they are half a turn apart.
help.sunlightbearing: Same as the dial above, but for light instead of shadows. They start half a turn apart like older versions. Match the numbers so light and shadows agree on where the sun is.
config.shadows.contacthardness.name: Sharp where it touches
config.shadows.contacthardness.tooltip: How much sharper a shadow is where it touches the ground than at its tip. This keeps thin shadows next to trunks and posts from blurring away. 0 gives the same softness all along, like before.
help.shadowcontacthardness: Makes shadows sharp where they touch the ground and softer toward the tip. 0 keeps the same softness all along, the old look.
config.shadows.penumbrastretch.name: Soft edge follows the light
config.shadows.penumbrastretch.tooltip: How much a shadow's soft edge stretches along the shadow, more when the sun is low. 0 keeps the old round edge. The overall softness stays the same.
help.shadowpenumbrastretch: Stretches a shadow's soft edge along the shadow when the sun is low, nearly round at midday. 0 keeps the round edge. It doesn't add blur, it only changes the shape.
